sources.title: Production of Large Computer Programs
sources.exact_locator: 1983 foreword; original paper Figure 4 and testing/documentation discussion, pp. 350–361
sources.claim_supported: Large-system staged engineering, controlled interfaces, successive testing, records and technical leadership pre-dated Royce; the retrospective reports prototyping and evolutionary learning.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: The prototype and claimed cost saving are retrospective recollections, not controlled evidence.

sources.title: Software Engineering: Report of a Conference Sponsored by the NATO Science Committee
sources.exact_locator: Design, simulation, feedback, limited initial systems and acceptance-testing discussions throughout the report
sources.claim_supported: The pre-Royce software-engineering conversation already included feedback, simulation, prototypes, limited releases and objective acceptance evidence.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: An edited record of heterogeneous views, not one prescribed method or outcome study.

sources.title: Managing the Development of Large Software Systems
sources.exact_locator: Figures 2–4; preliminary programme design; documentation; 'do it twice'; test planning; customer involvement
sources.claim_supported: Royce used a staged sequence as a problem setup, called the unmodified form risky, and proposed feedback, preliminary design, a pilot, early testing, documentation and customer review.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Experience-based management argument, not comparative causal evidence; still strongly staged and formal.

sources.author_organisation: Thomas E. Bell and Thomas A. Thayer
sources.title: Software Requirements: Are They Really a Problem?
sources.exact_locator: Figure 1; sections II–III
sources.claim_supported: An early published use of 'waterfall' for the Royce sequence and empirical evidence that requirements defects and changes persisted through development.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Does not prove the complete later textbook transmission chain or that the authors endorsed absolute one-pass development.

sources.title: Guidelines for Verifying and Validating Software Requirements and Design Specifications
sources.exact_locator: pp. 3–6: V-chart, requirement baseline, iterative V&V loops, problem reporting and testability criteria
sources.claim_supported: An early software V-chart pairs definition products with evaluation and explicitly includes iterative feedback and baseline correction.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: A V&V planning representation, not evidence that every V-shaped lifecycle shares this ancestry.

sources.author_organisation: David L. Parnas and Paul C. Clements
sources.title: A Rational Design Process: How and Why to Fake It
sources.exact_locator: Section II and documentation guidance, pp. 251–257
sources.claim_supported: Perfectly rational top-down chronology is impossible, but coherent, current design records still support review, transfer and maintenance.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Normative and analytic argument rather than comparative project-outcome evidence.

sources.title: No Silver Bullet—Essence and Accidents of Software Engineering
sources.exact_locator: Sections on requirements, prototyping and incremental development
sources.claim_supported: Complex systems require repeated user–designer interaction and evolutionary growth rather than complete one-shot specification.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Influential expert synthesis, not a controlled lifecycle comparison.

sources.title: A Spiral Model of Software Development and Enhancement
sources.exact_locator: Spiral-cycle quadrants and risk-driven model-selection discussion, pp. 61–72
sources.claim_supported: Risk rather than fixed phase order can determine prototyping, simulation, incremental construction and planning activities.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Does not show that all organisations can estimate or retire risk effectively.

sources.title: DOD-STD-2167A: Defense System Software Development
sources.exact_locator: Scope/application, development activities, reviews, configuration management and qualification testing
sources.claim_supported: The standard formally allowed tailoring, prototyping, overlap and recursive/iterative application while imposing ordered activities, data, reviews, baselines and approvals.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Textual permission to iterate does not establish how contracts and programmes implemented it.

sources.title: Controlling Software Projects
sources.exact_locator: Lifecycle control and V-shaped representation
sources.claim_supported: One influential software-engineering V-model formulation linked specification/design activities to corresponding test levels.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Shared diagram shape does not establish direct ancestry for systems Vee or German V-Modell.

sources.title: The Relationship of System Engineering to the Project Cycle
sources.exact_locator: Vee model and project-cycle discussion
sources.claim_supported: The systems-engineering Vee relates decomposition and definition to integration, verification and validation and presents systems engineering as through-life rather than a terminal phase.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: A conceptual model, not causal proof of project performance.

sources.title: Application of the 'Vee' to Incremental and Evolutionary Development
sources.exact_locator: Incremental/evolutionary Vee variants
sources.claim_supported: The systems Vee was explicitly applied to incremental and evolutionary development rather than being confined to one pass.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Shows conceptual compatibility, not that every Vee implementation is iterative.

sources.author_organisation: German Federal Government / V-Modell XT Bund
sources.title: V-Modell XT Bund
sources.exact_locator: Goals, glossary, tailoring, process modules, product states and conformance
sources.claim_supported: The German V-Modell is an integrated governance and project framework with modular tailoring, products, roles, decision points and change/problem management—not merely a V-shaped test diagram.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Conformance machinery can itself become process ceremony; current XT form does not prove earlier versions were equally flexible.

sources.title: Software Development and Documentation: Application and Reference Guidebook for MIL-STD-498
sources.exact_locator: Methodology independence, tailoring, information-item treatment and build strategies
sources.claim_supported: Engineering information and assurance obligations can be retained while decoupled from a mandatory document form or lifecycle order; grand-design, incremental and evolutionary builds are supported.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: A guide to applying a standard, not proof that contracting practice shed documentary burden.

sources.author_organisation: Craig Larman and Victor R. Basili
sources.title: Iterative and Incremental Development: A Brief History
sources.exact_locator: Historical cases and Royce discussion
sources.claim_supported: Iterative and incremental development existed in major aerospace/software programmes before the later Agile movement and Royce was widely simplified.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Secondary historical account, not causal comparison.

sources.author_organisation: Kai Petersen, Claes Wohlin and Dejan Baca
sources.title: The Waterfall Model in Large-Scale Development
sources.exact_locator: Ericsson case results on requirements, testing, versions and communication
sources.claim_supported: A real large-scale Waterfall implementation exhibited requirement waste, version confusion, late testing and organisational handoff problems.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Single telecom case; cannot establish universal effect sizes.

sources.title: Achieving Effective Acquisition of Information Technology in the Department of Defense
sources.exact_locator: Chapter 3, acquisition cycle, Waterfall assumptions, reviews and end-user feedback
sources.claim_supported: Real acquisition structures could preserve long-latency, approval-heavy Waterfall behaviour even when iterative development was nominally allowed.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Focused on DoD IT acquisition of its period, not all plan-driven engineering.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 — Systems and software engineering — System life cycle processes
sources.exact_locator: Scope, especially clauses describing iterative, concurrent and recursive use and non-prescription of a lifecycle model
sources.claim_supported: Modern systems-engineering lifecycle standards define process outcomes across the full lifecycle without prescribing one phase order, method, model or document format.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Normative framework; implementation quality and economic payoff depend on tailoring.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026 — Systems and software engineering — Software life cycle processes
sources.exact_locator: Scope, clauses 1 and introductory material on concurrent, iterative, recursive and incremental use and applicability to agile
sources.claim_supported: Software lifecycle obligations can be applied iteratively and incrementally and do not imply a fixed lifecycle model.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: The standard's statement that agile is believed more affordable/faster is contextual language, not an effect-size finding.

sources.title: IEEE 1012-2024 — Standard for System, Software, and Hardware Verification and Validation
sources.exact_locator: Scope and compatibility statement; integrity-level scaling
sources.claim_supported: V&V spans lifecycle processes, includes multiple evaluation methods, is compatible with all lifecycle models and scales by integrity.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Standardised requirements do not establish comparative benefit in every low-consequence project.

sources.title: IEEE 828-2012 — Standard for Configuration Management in Systems and Software Engineering
sources.exact_locator: Scope: identification, acquisition, change control, status, builds and releases
sources.claim_supported: Configuration management concerns item identity, change, status, build and release engineering, not merely document freezing.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Inactive-reserved edition and normative rather than empirical evidence.

sources.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook, NASA/SP-2016-6105 Rev. 2
sources.exact_locator: Sections 2.4, 5.3–5.5, 6.2–6.5 and review appendices
sources.claim_supported: Recursive/iterative systems engineering, verification/validation distinctions, qualification and acceptance, transition, requirements, interfaces, technical data and configuration management.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: NASA-specific guidance; formality and depth are explicitly to be tailored.

sources.title: Configuration Management — NASA Systems Engineering Handbook web chapter
sources.exact_locator: Section 6.5, especially true representation, integrity and unsafe release warning
sources.claim_supported: CM provides visibility of the true product representation and integrity by identifying and controlling baseline changes.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Normative rationale; does not quantify net benefit.

sources.title: Interface Management — NASA Systems Engineering Handbook web chapter
sources.exact_locator: Section 6.3 outputs: interface documents, approvals, assumptions and anomalies
sources.claim_supported: Interface definitions, ownership, approved changes and rationale coordinate separately controlled system elements.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Formal unanimous approval is suitable only where both sides truly share interface authority; it can bottleneck local change.

sources.author_organisation: NASA Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board
sources.title: Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report
sources.exact_locator: Root-cause and contributing-cause findings concerning English/metric units, navigation software, communication and verification
sources.claim_supported: Interface semantics, cross-team communication and system-level verification can fail despite local component work, with mission-level consequences.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: One highly specific mishap; does not prove that an ICD or board alone would have prevented it.

sources.author_organisation: RTCA Forum for Aeronautical Software / EUROCAE
sources.title: FTP 1050 Rev. 3 — Compliance with DO-178C/ED-12C and DO-278A/ED-109A Using Agile Methodology
sources.exact_locator: pp. 3–6: lifecycle neutrality, transition criteria, evidence packaging, baselines, change impact and bidirectional traceability
sources.claim_supported: High-assurance aerospace objectives can coexist with iterative development; certification credit remains baseline-, evidence-, trace- and independence-sensitive.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Informational/educational paper, expressly not guidance and not the DO-178C standard itself.

sources.title: Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality Management System Software
sources.exact_locator: Risk-based assurance, least-burdensome evidence, testing versus other assurance activities and continuous monitoring
sources.claim_supported: Regulated software assurance can be scaled to intended use and risk rather than maximising scripted evidence uniformly.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Applies to production and quality-management-system software, not all medical-device product software.

sources.title: ISO 26262 — Road vehicles — Functional safety
sources.exact_locator: Lifecycle parts covering management, concept, system, hardware, software, production/operation/service/decommission and ASIL-oriented analyses
sources.claim_supported: Automotive functional-safety controls scale with hazard classification and span lifecycle, configuration, change and evidence.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Automotive electrical/electronic functional safety; not a general software lifecycle prescription.

sources.author_organisation: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe
sources.title: UN Regulation No. 156 — Software Update and Software Update Management System
sources.date_version: In force from 2021; current consolidated text as applicable
sources.exact_locator: Software update management system, vehicle identification, update integrity and manufacturer obligations
sources.claim_supported: Operational software updates can require controlled identity, compatibility, authority and through-life records even when delivered incrementally.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Type-approval regime for vehicles; does not justify equal controls for ordinary reversible software.

sources.title: Common Safety Method for Risk Evaluation and Assessment
sources.date_version: Current ERA guidance and Regulation (EU) No 402/2013 as amended
sources.exact_locator: Significant-change assessment, hazard record, risk acceptance and independent assessment-body guidance
sources.claim_supported: Rail changes are assessed for significance and risk, with independent assessment intensity proportionate to risk and evidence extending beyond paperwork.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Rail-specific legal scheme; 'significance' tests and assessment roles are not universal.

sources.title: 10 CFR 50.59 — Changes, Tests, and Experiments
sources.exact_locator: Evaluation criteria distinguishing changes allowed without prior approval from those requiring licence amendment
sources.claim_supported: Nuclear configuration change control is graded: licensees may make some evaluated changes without prior regulator approval, while threshold-crossing changes require it.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: A nuclear licensing rule; not evidence that all changes need a standing external board.

sources.title: DOE O 425.1E — Verification of Readiness to Start Up or Restart Nuclear Facilities
sources.exact_locator: Applicability, contractor/DOE readiness reviews, scope and startup/restart approval
sources.claim_supported: High-hazard nuclear startup/restart requires evidence that the actual facility, people, procedures and controls are ready before operational authority is granted.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: High-hazard nuclear facilities only; exact ceremony should not be transplanted.

sources.title: Manual of Air System Safety Cases (MASSC), Issue 3
sources.exact_locator: Chapters 1–3, especially safety-case theory, argument/evidence primacy, through-life use and implementation pathologies
sources.claim_supported: A safety case is a living structured argument and evidence, not merely its report; static, compliance-only, self-confirming and late-created cases are recognised failure modes.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Guidance documents benefits and pathologies but does not supply strong comparative outcome estimates.

sources.author_organisation: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: SP 800-218 — Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
sources.exact_locator: Framework scope and practice groups
sources.claim_supported: Security practices are high-level outcomes designed for integration into any SDLC rather than a separate mandatory phase sequence.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Practice framework, not proof that checklist adoption achieves security.

sources.title: Software Developmental Test and Evaluation in DevSecOps Guidebook
sources.exact_locator: Executive summary; sections 1.1–1.4; continuous T&E, roles, data reuse, independent OT&E
sources.claim_supported: Testing can become an early, continuous, automated continuum while preserving decision authority and independent operational evaluation.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Guidance and intended operating model; actual programme adoption and outcome evidence vary.

sources.author_organisation: U.S. Department of Defense Chief Information Officer
sources.title: DevSecOps Continuous Authorization to Operate (cATO) Implementation Guide
sources.exact_locator: Continuous risk determination, evidence dashboards, risk tolerances, authorising official and residual-risk roles
sources.claim_supported: Operational authorisation can consume continuous evidence and monitoring rather than rely only on episodic packages, while retaining explicit risk acceptance authority.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Continuous evidence can continuously reproduce weak controls; authority and measurement quality remain critical.

sources.title: Systems Engineering Guidebook
sources.exact_locator: Tailoring, technical baselines, event-driven technical reviews, entrance/exit criteria and digital engineering
sources.claim_supported: Modern defence systems engineering treats reviews as event/evidence driven and lifecycle processes as tailored rather than fixed calendar phases.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Programme implementation may still game milestones or duplicate reviews.

sources.title: Authoritative Sources of Truth Study (WRT-1051) Final Technical Report
sources.exact_locator: Findings on 'authoritative source of truth' ambiguity, interoperability, governance, workflows and culture
sources.claim_supported: Digital-authority initiatives can fail through ambiguous authority, tool interoperability, semantics, access and governance rather than document format alone.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Exploratory research and practice synthesis rather than controlled outcome evaluation.

sources.title: Value and Benefits of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Evidence from the Literature
sources.exact_locator: Results and evidence-classification sections, Systems Engineering 24(1), pp. 51–66
sources.claim_supported: Many claimed MBSE benefits are perceived or expected rather than measured; measured comparative evidence is sparse.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Publication evidence may omit internal programme metrics and newer implementations.

sources.author_organisation: Edward R. Carroll and Robert J. Malins
sources.title: Systematic Literature Review: How Is Model-Based Systems Engineering Justified?
sources.exact_locator: Case-study coding and evidence tables
sources.claim_supported: MBSE case literature reports many benefits, but metric quality and case comparability are heterogeneous.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Review included practitioner cases of variable rigour and predates current toolchains.

sources.title: Assessing the Effect of Requirements Traceability for Software Maintenance
sources.exact_locator: Method and results: 52 participants, 315 maintenance tasks
sources.claim_supported: Under experimentally supplied, correct and complete links, traceability improved task speed and correctness.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Mostly students, unfamiliar systems, ideal traces and no full measurement of trace-creation/maintenance cost.

sources.title: Do Developers Benefit from Requirements Traceability When Evolving and Maintaining a Software System?
sources.exact_locator: Empirical Software Engineering 20, experimental results
sources.claim_supported: Replication found participants with traceability approximately 24% faster and solutions approximately 50% more correct.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Task-level laboratory evidence; link quality and lifecycle maintenance costs remain external.

sources.title: Preventing Defects: The Impact of Requirements Traceability Completeness on Software Quality
sources.exact_locator: 24 open-source projects, 610 components; trace-completeness/defect analyses
sources.claim_supported: Completeness for several development activities was statistically associated with lower defect rates.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Observational association, project selection and confounding prevent a simple causal claim.

sources.author_organisation: Fangchao Tian, Tianlu Wang, Peng Liang, Chong Wang, Arif Ali Khan and Muhammad Ali Babar
sources.title: The Impact of Traceability on Software Maintenance and Evolution: A Mapping Study
sources.exact_locator: Synthesis of 63 studies published 2000–2020
sources.claim_supported: Change management is the most common benefit; establishing and maintaining links is the principal cost; strong industrial evidence remains needed.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Maps heterogeneous studies and does not yield universal cost-benefit thresholds.

sources.author_organisation: Dolores R. Wallace and Roger U. Fujii, NIST
sources.title: Software Verification and Validation: Its Role in Computer Assurance and Its Relationship with Software Project Management Standards
sources.exact_locator: Recommended V&V tasks and comparative-study discussion, especially pp. 7 and 16
sources.claim_supported: V&V should start early and focus on critical areas; comparative case results show both possible savings and substantial cost/coordination burdens.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Older projects, non-equivalent comparisons and substantial methodological uncertainty.

sources.title: An Assessment of Space Shuttle Flight Software Development Processes
sources.exact_locator: Chapter 2, IV&V objectives, scope and independence
sources.claim_supported: IV&V scope should scale to criticality and latent-error consequence; technical, managerial and financial independence trade against timeliness and access.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Committee judgement and testimony, not a clean causal estimate.

sources.author_organisation: Bill Haskins, Jonette Stecklein, Brandon Dick, Gregory Moroney, Randy Lovell and James Dabney
sources.title: Error Cost Escalation Through the Project Life Cycle
sources.exact_locator: Three methods and correction-cost multipliers for aerospace-like systems
sources.claim_supported: Correction costs can rise steeply where hardware/software system commitments, rework and verification accumulate.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Multipliers vary enormously by method and domain and are not a universal software law.

sources.author_organisation: Tim Menzies, William Nichols, Forrest Shull and Lucas Layman
sources.title: Are Delayed Issues Harder to Resolve? Revisiting Cost-to-Fix of Defects throughout the Lifecycle
sources.exact_locator: 171 software projects, delay/cost analyses and conclusions
sources.claim_supported: No consistent, substantial global delayed-issue effect was found; late discovery is not automatically exponentially expensive.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Issue-tracker measures do not capture every physical, certification, contractual or operational consequence.

sources.title: What's Next? After Stage-Gate
sources.exact_locator: Critique of traditional linear/bureaucratic Stage-Gate and next-generation overlapping, adaptive, risk-based forms
sources.claim_supported: Even the Stage-Gate tradition recognised bureaucratic linearity and evolved toward context-specific, overlapping, build-test-feedback operation.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Written by the method's principal advocate; outcome evidence is not independently established by the article.

sources.author_organisation: Mark Keil, Joan Mann and Arun Rai
sources.title: Why Software Projects Escalate: An Empirical Analysis and Test of Four Theoretical Models
sources.exact_locator: MIS Quarterly 24(4), escalation-model tests
sources.claim_supported: Sunk cost, project factors and psychological/social dynamics can sustain failing software projects.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Does not show that all formal reviews increase escalation; effective stop authority may reduce it.

sources.title: A Systematic Review of Software Development Cost Estimation Studies
sources.exact_locator: Review of 304 estimation papers
sources.claim_supported: Software-estimation research is fragmented and context-dependent; no single predictive technique warrants universal confidence.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Literature through 2004; does not imply that forecasting is useless.

sources.title: Evidence-Based Guidelines for Assessment of Software Development Cost Uncertainty
sources.exact_locator: Guidelines and empirical basis for overconfidence, outside views, multiple sources and feedback
sources.claim_supported: Point estimates and narrow intervals are often overconfident; structured uncertainty, independent views and feedback improve decision quality.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Guidelines improve epistemic discipline but do not eliminate political or irreducible uncertainty.

sources.title: GAO Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide: Best Practices for Developing and Managing Program Costs
sources.exact_locator: Risk/sensitivity analysis, assumptions, independent estimate and update-with-actuals practices
sources.claim_supported: Mature predictive planning uses explicit assumptions, uncertainty, risk, independent challenge and actuals rather than treating one baseline estimate as truth.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Best-practice guidance; compliance with the guide does not assure forecast accuracy.

sources.author_organisation: Mojtaba Shahin, Muhammad Ali Babar and Liming Zhu
sources.title: Continuous Integration, Delivery and Deployment: A Systematic Review on Approaches, Tools, Challenges and Practices
sources.exact_locator: Synthesis of 69 studies
sources.claim_supported: CI/CD provides rapid integration and feedback but depends on automation, test quality, architecture, environments and organisational capability.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Heterogeneous evidence and publication bias; continuous delivery does not itself establish assurance.

sources.title: Continuous Integration and Delivery: A Systematic Review
sources.exact_locator: Review of empirical CI/CD studies, benefits and challenges
sources.claim_supported: CI/CD can improve feedback and release performance, but infrastructure, flaky tests, integration complexity and adoption costs are recurrent constraints.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Effects depend on context and measurement; not a safety-certification study.

sources.author_organisation: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: SP 800-34 Rev. 1 — Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems
sources.exact_locator: Business impact analysis, recovery strategies, plans, testing and maintenance
sources.claim_supported: Recovery and contingency are engineering capabilities that require preconditions and exercises, not merely an emergency document.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Federal information-system focus and older edition.

sources.title: Operational Readiness Review — Systems Engineering Handbook Appendix
sources.exact_locator: Operational Readiness Review definition and success criteria
sources.claim_supported: Readiness concerns the actual deployed hardware, software, people, procedures, support and user documentation—not document approval alone.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: NASA review form is not universally required; the underlying actual-state readiness property is.

sources.title: Weapon System Sustainment: DOD's Sustainment Reviews and Cost-Growth Information
sources.exact_locator: Findings on sustainment baselines, cost-growth determination and causes
sources.claim_supported: Absent or weak sustainment baselines can prevent authorities from determining growth and acting on obsolescence, supply and support problems.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Defence weapon-system setting; baseline reporting can itself be gamed or burdensome.

sources.author_organisation: Jennifer Whyte, Anna Stasis and Carmel Lindkvist
sources.title: Managing Change in the Delivery of Complex Projects: Configuration Management, Asset Information and 'Big Data'
sources.exact_locator: Cross-case analysis involving complex aerospace/infrastructure organisations
sources.claim_supported: Digital asset information becomes a contractual/operational deliverable and configuration/change practices coordinate complex project state.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Qualitative cross-case research; does not quantify causal return.

sources.title: Weapon Systems Annual Assessment and Knowledge-Based Acquisition Series
sources.exact_locator: Knowledge at programme start, design maturity, production and testing findings
sources.claim_supported: Large physical programmes incur risk when technology, design, supplier and production commitments outrun demonstrated knowledge.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Association in defence acquisitions; stage labels and reviews alone do not create knowledge.

sources.title: Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR)
sources.exact_locator: Effective-date, ISO 13485 incorporation, lifecycle/design controls and risk-management discussion
sources.claim_supported: Medical-device quality controls are through-life and risk-based within a regulatory authority framework.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Regulatory applicability is limited to covered device manufacturers and products.

sources.title: Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) Overview
sources.exact_locator: Technical, managerial and financial independence dimensions
sources.claim_supported: Independence is multidimensional and cannot be inferred from a different reviewer name alone.
sources.contrary_evidence_or_limit: Programme rationale, not comparative economics.
